claims.statement: The official BDO transfer-card manual documents a stateful workflow in which the receiving waste holder confirms takeover or rejects the card and returns it for correction.

The same official manual gives the transporter a bounded role and records transport confirmation, date, vehicle, waste code, transferor, and recipient, making a role-signed field preflight technically plausible.

contrary_evidence: BDO itself already records the legally relevant statuses and parties.
Generic waste-management software may already solve this for large operators.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: one receiving site can pull multiple carriers and waste producers into the workflow.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 1000 fleets or installer accounts averaging 699 PLN monthly would exceed 8 million PLN ARR; a profitable, founder-owned network at that scale could support more than 5 million PLN of founder net worth in years 5 to 8.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 15 hours weekly for one waste stream and one carrier integration before expansion.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 75% gross margin after mobile support and evidence storage.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: channel-led acquisition repays within four months at 699 PLN monthly and 70% contribution margin.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 9 PLN per released handoff or 699 PLN per fleet-month.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: every regulated pickup repeats the transaction and preserves the shared ledger.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A correction graph across waste codes, site types, carriers, receivers, and rejection reasons
fingerprint.customer: Small and midsize Polish construction, HVAC, solar, and battery installers plus their waste carriers
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Waste receiving sites, carrier fleets, installer wholesalers, and environmental-accounting firms invite downstream crews
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Per-handoff mobile chain-of-custody software with fleet subscriptions
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The waste producer or carrier pays when a QR handoff is released and later reconciles to a completed transfer
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Waste is about to leave a job site and the transfer record must be valid and receivable

founder_fit: The family renewable company offers a bounded route to observe real waste handoffs.
Computer vision can assist evidence capture while deterministic rules retain control.
The product minimizes founder-facing sales by using carriers and waste sites as channels.
risks: Offline sites and hurried drivers may bypass the field token.
Incorrect waste-code suggestions could create regulatory exposure.
The payer may be fragmented across waste producer, carrier, and receiver.

structure.control_point: Role-signed QR release at physical waste pickup before the vehicle departs
structure.critical_dependency: Field adoption and reliable synchronization with the official BDO record

thesis: A mobile chain-of-custody layer for renewable and construction crews could prevent a skip, pallet, or hazardous component from leaving a job until the BDO waste-transfer card, vehicle, carrier, photos, and receiving site agree. It would preserve an auditable QR handoff and synchronize the official record rather than replacing BDO.
title: BDO Waste Handoff Token for Field Crews
uncertainties: The official integration options and permitted automation scope need verification.
The rate of rejected or retrospectively corrected cards among small installers is unknown.
The 48000 PLN capital figure and all pricing or scale figures below are hypotheses.
